ai.description: Terai Tree Frogs reach 5–8 cm. They are yellowish-brown with dark dorsal spots and a distinct white line along the upper lip. Key features include webbing on the feet and prominent toe discs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Polypedates teraiensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-colored, X-shaped or hourglass-like pattern on its dorsum, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Terai tree frog inhabits moist deciduous forests and agricultural landscapes in the Himalayan foothills, typically ranging from lowlands up to 1,500 meters in altitude.
ai.behavior: The Terai Tree Frog is primarily nocturnal and exhibits a unique defensive strategy by secreting a frothy mucus to protect its eggs from desiccation and predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Polypedates teraiensis* is an oviparous breeder that constructs foam nests above water. Breeding occurs during the monsoon (June–August), with clutches of 100–300 eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Polypedates teraiensis* is found across the Himalayan foothills and Terai regions of northern India, ranging from Uttarakhand through West Bengal to the Northeast states.
ai.callDescription: The Terai Tree Frog produces a series of rapid, high-pitched "chick-chick" notes, typically heard calling from vegetation near stagnant water bodies or monsoon pools.
